column1: # Wiki image hold_ack ledger. Mirrors the vendor-tree hold_ack contract in
# when a wiki image's pinned CM044 sha sits behind live main HEAD -- the pin is
# treated as HELD (non-fatal) only if EVERY delta commit is listed here AND a
# written reason is given AND shipping_bugfixes_grafted is asserted true.
# Any un-acknowledged delta commit stays fail-closed RED, exactly like the
#   pinned_sha_prefix          8+ hex prefix of the CM044 source sha recorded
#                              digest. Row matches only if the current pin
#                              still starts with this prefix (defensive: a
#                              re-pin invalidates the ack, forcing a re-decision).
#   hold_ack_shas              Space-separated delta commits between the pin
#                              and live CM044 main HEAD (short or full hex).
#   shipping_bugfixes_grafted  Explicit human assertion: "true" if the
#                              bugfixes among the held commits are grafted
#                              into the shipped artefact by other means, or
#                              the next re-baseline. Empty / false = RED.
#   reason                     Written justification for the hold. REQUIRED --
#                              an empty reason keeps the pin RED.
# Comment lines (# or blank) are ignored. Multi-line values NOT supported;
# keep the reason to a single line (semicolons for structure).

column1: # v1.0.17 (2026-08-07 ORM). Pin c4448cc (= CM044 tag v0.1.5, the #165 design-system merge) sits 2 commits behind CM044 main f949872. Both delta commits are PROVABLY outside both Docker build contexts, so a rebuild would produce byte-identical image content -- this ack is discharged by a mechanical argument, not by a promise. It also cannot fossilise: the moment CM044 main gains a commit touching compiler/ or mkdocs/, that new sha is not in hold_ack_shas and this gate goes RED again.

NO bugfix is held: the delta is release tooling and its runbook, zero shipping-surface change. Image content independently verified against c4448cc by file hash (compiler/pages/dashboard.py, compiler/pages/person_pages.py, compiler/locale.py all sha256-identical to git) and all 11 cut_markers wiki assertions PASS against this digest.

v1.0.19 (2026-08-11 ORM). Delta to CM044 main is exactly two commits, fb6fd8c2 (#182 run the test suite) and c9bc2565 (#183 assert the suite actually ran), and between them they touch exactly TWO files: .github/workflows/tests.yml (added) and requirements-test.txt (added). NO BUGFIX IS HELD, which is what shipping_bugfixes_grafted asserts. VERIFIED rather than asserted from the v1.0.17 precedent: docker/Dockerfile.compiler at CM044 main carries exactly two COPY lines, "COPY requirements.txt ." and "COPY compiler/ ./compiler/". Neither .github/ nor requirements-test.txt is in that build context -- note requirements.txt and requirements-test.txt are different files -- so a rebuild from main yields byte-identical image content and re-pinning would change the digest without changing a single shipped byte.

v1.0.19 (2026-08-11 ORM). Same two-commit CI-only delta as the wiki-compiler row above. VERIFIED at CM044 main: docker/Dockerfile.site COPYs mkdocs/mkdocs.yml, mkdocs/overrides, three named compiler files (identity_label.py, render_wiki_title.py, html_sanitise.py) and docker/wiki-site-serve.py. Zero intersection with .github/workflows/ or requirements-test.txt, so the site image is likewise byte-identical when rebuilt from main. NO BUGFIX IS HELD.

v1.0.27 (2026-08-15 ORM). Delta from the pinned 7d6431fb to CM044 main 63efbc76 is exactly TWO commits and BOTH touch a single file, .github/workflows/release-images.yml, and nothing else: 992a010 (fix(release): verify the artefact instead of announcing it) and 63efbc7 (ci(release-images): build arm64 only). MEASURED with git show --name-only per commit, not read off the titles. THAT FILE IS COPIED INTO NEITHER IMAGE, which is the whole basis of this ack and is checked against the Dockerfiles rather than assumed: docker/Dockerfile.compiler copies requirements.txt and compiler/ only; docker/Dockerfile.site copies mkdocs/mkdocs.yml, mkdocs/overrides, three named compiler/*.py (identity_label, render_wiki_title, html_sanitise) and docker/wiki-site-serve.py. A workflow file is in neither set, so the pinned digests are byte-for-byte what these two commits would still produce, and rebuilding would change nothing but the digest. Same shape as the fd47239 docs-only row above. shipping_bugfixes_grafted STAYS TRUE HONESTLY: neither commit contains customer-facing wiki behaviour. 992a010 hardens the RELEASE JOB (verify the artefact rather than announce it); 63efbc7 drops linux/amd64 from the build matrix, which changes what a FUTURE release publishes, not what the pinned images contain. SELF-INFLICTED, and worth naming for whoever hits this next: 63efbc7 is the ORM's own CM044 PR #206, merged minutes after the wiki re-pin. Landing a CM044 change of ANY kind re-reds this gate immediately, because the gate re-enumerates the delta against live HEAD and finds shas it has not been told about. That is the gate working, not failing, and it is the wiki-side twin of the upstream-plus-graft double-ack already recorded for vendor:doctor. The arm64 intent is separately enforced at the ARTEFACT by tests/test_pinned_wiki_images_are_arm64_only.sh, so this ack does not carry that guarantee on trust.
